learningObjective: Identify correct properties of differential testing (running two implementations of the same spec on many random inputs and comparing outputs) versus golden testing.

canonicalClaims.claim: Differential testing compares two independent implementations on many random inputs to surface corner-case bugs; usable differential testing must record inputs so failures are reproducible.
conditions: The two implementations are truly independent.
The framework records seeds and states of triggering inputs.
nonImplications: Does not imply bit equality is required between implementations.
Does not imply golden testing is obsolete.

misconceptions.claim: Any discrepancy between eager and compiled PyTorch is a bug.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Compiler reordering can change low-order bits; tolerance is expected.
Golden tests document known-hard cases and provide deterministic reproducibility.

misconceptions.claim: Random inputs alone are sufficient for coverage.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Random distributions may miss adversarial or structural cases; targeted inputs still matter.

misconceptions.claim: Diff-tests need not record seeds because failures are exposed on rerun.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Without seeds, reruns produce different random inputs; failures become non-reproducible.
